(a) 
Any person required to file a return or report or perform any act under the provisions of this title who shall fail or neglect to file such return or report or perform such act within the time required shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined not more than $300 for each and every failure or neglect. The penalty provided herein shall be in addition to the other penalties provided in this title.
 
    (b) 
Any person required to file a return or report or perform any act under the provisions of this title who willfully fails or refuses to file such return or report or perform such act within the time required shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined not more than $5,000 or imprisoned for not more than one year, or both. The penalty provided herein shall be in addition to the other penalties provided in this title.

fable.w: The section only sets criminal penalties (fines and imprisonment) for failing to file required returns or reports. The tempting reading is that private persons filing reports with the government amounts to outside involvement, but that is a compliance duty, not consultation on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or grant of a right to sue.
fable.s: Any person required to file a return or report or perform any act under the provisions of this title who shall fail or neglect to file such return or report or perform such act within the time required shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined not more than $300 for each and every failure or neglect.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes criminal penalties (fines and imprisonment) for individuals who fail to file tax returns or reports. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The interaction described is enforcement of compliance, not participation in decision-making.
qwen_block.s: Any person required to file a return or report or perform any act under the provisions of this title who shall fail or neglect to file such return or report or perform such act within the time required shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined not more than $300 for each and every failure or neglect.

opus.w: This section only sets criminal fines and prison terms for failing to file required returns or reports. It is tempting to treat filing a report with the government as outsiders taking part. But filing is a compliance duty, not consultation before a federal decision. Nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty or right to challenge a federal decision.
opus.s: Any person required to file a return or report or perform any act under the provisions of this title who shall fail or neglect to file such return or report or perform such act within the time required shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined not more than $300 for each and every failure or neglect.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines criminal penalties for failing to file tax returns or reports. It does not establish a process for outside parties to consult with or influence federal decision-making. The definition of participation excludes mere compliance obligations and focuses on consultation, advisory roles, or rights to object/sue regarding decisions. This is a penalty provision, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: Any person required to file a return or report or perform any act under the provisions of this title who shall fail or neglect to file such return or report or perform such act within the time required shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined not more than $300 for each and every failure or neglect.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement to "file a return or report" constitutes participation because it involves an outside party interacting with the government. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and generally treats compliance with reporting obligations as distinct from participatory decision-making processes like advisory boards or public comment periods. Furthermore, this section is purely punitive, defining criminal penalties for non-compliance, rather than establishing a mechanism for outside input into federal decisions.
